newsitem.title: USA: Cochran lawyers file final brief in fraud case.
newsitem.headline: Cochran lawyers file final brief in fraud case.

text.p: Lawyers for former Oklahoma investment banker Robert Cochran, convicted May 3 of cheating two municipal authorities on bond deals, filed a final brief Wednesday urging a U.S. appeals court to vacate that ruling.

The brief tells a three-member panel of the Tenth U.S. Court of Appeals that the ex-vice president of Stifel, Nicolaus & Co never harmed the municipal authorities and, therefore, should not have been convicted of wire fraud.
"To have wire fraud, you have to have some intent to harm the alleged victims," Cochran lawyer B.J. Rothbaum told Reuters in a telephone interview where he summarized the brief.

"The Oklahoma City Airport Trust Authority and Sisters of St. Mary Health Care Authority (were not) harmed. They didn't lose money. They made money. It was a beneficial deal," Rothbaum said, referring to the two bond issuers cited in the government's case against Cochran.
But Susan Cox, assistant U.S. attorney on the case and author of an October 30 government brief, said Cochran's actions were "ordinary garden variety fraud."
Cox said, "There is intent to deceive and, thus, a scheme to defraud."
A federal jury May 4 convicted Cochran on eight of 21 counts of cheating the two authorities.

In late August, U.S. District Judge Ralph Thompson sentenced Cochran to seven years and three months in prison and ordered him to return $629,000 in illegal profits on a $76.7 million airport issue and a $265 million healthcare authority deal.
Cochran was to report to El Reno Correctional Institution in Oklahoma on Sept 30. But the appeals panel on Sept 26 granted him an emergency delay.
The judges wanted more time to review an August decision by lower court Judge Thompson to deny a request by Cochran to be released on bail pending his appeal.
Cochran's attorneys filed their first brief in the appeal on Oct 15.
